scope_limitation.statement: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' (champions, levels, ranks, full loadouts, fight window, roster composition) does NOT exist anywhere inside the permitted evidence tree. Exhaustive search of the export (case-insensitive grep for 'cleaver_bloodsong', 'coupled_scenarios', 'roster' over every file under data/) returns no scenario tuple; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json holds a different, unrelated corpus. The golden inputs live under scripts/, which this runbook forbids.
scope_limitation.consequence: A bit-exact independent reproduction of 4041.9 is impossible from the permitted sources. What follows is therefore a rule-level oracle: the governing wiki rules are quoted and checked, and the observed delta is decomposed and tested for consistency/magnitude against every mechanic the scenario name puts in play.
scope_limitation.honest_label: partial verification (rule + direction + magnitude), not a full numeric reproduction

sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
Non-{{tip|basic damage}} dealt on the same target may apply stacks only once per frame.

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json (corroboration of the {{rd|...}} template convention = melee value first, ranged value second)
sources_quoted.text: Ravenous Hydra / Tiamat {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}; Death's Dance {{rd|30%|10%}}; Serpent's Fang {{rd|50%|35%}} — the last is independently glossed in data/worklists/e8b-task.md line 15 as 'REDUCES SHIELDS ... by 50%/35% (melee/ranged)'. Hence Bloodsong's Expose Weakness = 8% amp for a melee holder, 5% for a ranged holder.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 2.3 item 2 (Black Cleaver average stacks)
sources_quoted.text: the established model uses a fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes ... Recommendation: replace the constant with the closed-form Cesaro mean when a champion module needs exact BC numbers
m(R) = 100 / (100 + R) (apply_resistance, resistance.py); EHP round-trip raw = post*(1+R/100)

observed_delta.note: 4074.9 - 4041.9 = 33.0 exactly; -0.80984% of the old value. This is a fine-grained refinement, not the removal of an effect (see magnitude_discriminator).

hypothesis_H1_bloodsong_expose_weakness_.rule: Expose Weakness amplifies the target's damage taken from all sources by 8% (melee holder) / 5% (ranged holder), 4 s, 1.5 s internal cooldown.
hypothesis_H1_bloodsong_expose_weakness_.model: leaf = U + A*(1+a), U = damage outside the 4 s Expose Weakness window, A = un-amplified damage inside it, a = amp.
hypothesis_H1_bloodsong_expose_weakness_.assessment: Self-consistent, and the implied amplified base lands exactly on 1100.0 rather than anywhere in the 1098.3-1101.7 band the 0.1-rounding permits. A ~29% amplified share is what a 4 s debuff window inside a longer coupled fight looks like. Correcting a melee 8% to the sourced ranged 5% is a strict decrease -> matches the observed direction.

hypothesis_H2_black_cleaver_carve_averag.rule: Carve = 6% armor reduction per stack, cap 5 stacks (30%), 6 s. Mitigation m(R) = 100/(100+R).
hypothesis_H2_black_cleaver_carve_averag.model: old stacks = 0.8*5 = 4 -> 24% reduction; new = exact Cesaro mean C - C(C-1)/(2h) = 5 - 10/h.
hypothesis_H2_black_cleaver_carve_averag.assessment: Also self-consistent: across every realistic post-penetration armor the delta corresponds to roughly one third of a Carve stack, i.e. the Cesaro mean at h ~ 7-8 hits — exactly the regime docs/math-foundations.md says the 0.8*C constant overstates (the constant equals the exact mean only at ~10 hits, and overstates for h < 10). A secondary roster target taking 7-8 hits is the natural h. Correcting toward the exact mean at h < 10 is a strict decrease -> matches the observed direction.

hypothesis_H3_per_target_debuff_scoping.rule: Both mechanics are per-target debuffs in the cached wiki text: Carve applies 'to an enemy champion' and stacks per that champion; Expose Weakness 'inflict THEM' for 4 s. Neither is a global/roster-wide state.
hypothesis_H3_per_target_debuff_scoping.consequence: In a multi-enemy roster, a secondary target (breakdown[2]) that receives fewer physical hits must carry fewer Carve stacks, and receives Expose Weakness only if the Bloodsong holder's empowered attack actually landed on it. Any correction from shared/global state toward per-target state lowers the secondary target's damage.
hypothesis_H3_per_target_debuff_scoping.assessment: Direction matches. No wiki text in the export supports a roster-wide reading of either debuff.

magnitude_discriminator.purpose: Distinguish a legitimate refinement (down) from a regression that wrongly deletes a real effect (also down).

computed.case: Expose Weakness removed outright (8% -> 0%) on a fully amplified leaf

magnitude_discriminator.conclusion: The observed change is an order of magnitude smaller than any 'effect deleted' outcome. It is consistent only with a fine correction — a fractional Carve stack, or the melee->ranged amp step applied over a partial window — not with an effect being wrongly dropped.

reasoning: Every mechanic the scenario id puts in play (Black Cleaver Carve, Bloodsong Expose Weakness) was checked against its cached wiki text, and every correction those texts license moves the leaf DOWN, never up: the ranged amp is 5% not 8%; the exact Cesaro mean of the capped Carve ramp is below 0.8*C for fights shorter than ~10 hits; and both debuffs are per-target, so a secondary roster target cannot inherit a leading target's stacks or amp.

The two quantitative hypotheses each reproduce the -33.0 delta with parameters in a plausible physical range (H1: an exactly-1100.0 amplified base, a ~29% amplified share; H2: ~1/3 of a Carve stack, h ~ 7-8 hits at any realistic armor).
The delta's magnitude (0.81%) rules out the main competing story in which the change is a regression that deleted a legitimate effect; those cases all land at 7-11%.
No source in the permitted evidence tree supports the higher value 4074.9 over the lower value 4041.9 under any reading.
caveats: This receipt does NOT independently reproduce 4041.9 numerically; the scenario input tuple is outside the permitted evidence tree (see scope_limitation).

H1 and H2 are not discriminated by the available evidence — both fit the delta. The verdict does not depend on which one is the actual change, because both point the same direction and both favour the new value.

To upgrade this to a full verification, an oracle would need the scenario's champion/level/rank/item/roster tuple and target armor, which would have to be supplied as data rather than read from scripts/.
